title: Our AI Game video demo -- Ever Shift Wondering
author: Game2Entertainment

comments.author: Leoporix
comments.body: Are the AI systems hosted locally?

replies.author: Game2Entertainment
replies.body:
Hi, Sorry for the late reply!   
Our team has been heads-down working on the game over the past few months, so we haven’t had much time to check Reddit.

Here is our experience:  
Right now, we’re using the GPT and Gemini APIs rather than running the models locally.

We actually spent quite a bit of time exploring local models as well. We managed to get them running successfully with Ollama and ComfyUI, but we ran into a number of issues. Things like   
1. users’ hardware requirements   
2. the trade-off between model size and quality  
3. whether a model needs its own fine-tuning/optimization  
4. the fact that different models can require very different prompt strategies and agent setups all make supporting local models quite complicated.

After testing and thinking through the trade-offs, we feel that local models could be a great option for more advanced users who want to choose and configure their own models. That’s something we may open up in the future, but it’s not available in our game yet.

For a general user, we currently feel that local models still come with too many hardware and configuration barriers, so API-based models are the more practical choice for us for now.
